name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Jason Wei, Xuezhi Wang, Dale Schuurmans, Maarten Bosma, Brian Ichter, Fei Xia, Ed H. Chi, Quoc V. Le, Denny Zhou et al. — Google Research, Brain Team
venue: NeurIPS 2022 (36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); originally arXiv 2201.11903 (Jan 2022)
code_url: No official code release; prompts/exemplars provided in the paper appendix (Appendix G, H, Tables 20-21). PaLM/LaMDA models not publicly released.
reflection_type: none — CoT prompting is not a reflection/self-correction method. It elicits a single forward pass of intermediate reasoning steps; no critique, verification, or revision loop. It is a precursor substrate that later reflective methods (Self-Refine, Reflexion) build on.
feedback_source: none — no feedback signal is used. The model generates a chain of thought from few-shot exemplars and reads off the final answer in a single greedy decode; there is no self-generated critique, tool, unit test, or oracle feedback.
iteration_structure: single-shot — one forward generation per problem (greedy decoding). No iterative refinement, retry, or search. (The authors note follow-up work on self-consistency adds sampling/majority vote, but that is outside this paper.)
reflection_object: reasoning chain — the method augments the model's output with an explicit series of intermediate natural-language reasoning steps (the chain of thought) before the final answer. It modifies output content by inserting a reasoning trace, but does not reflect on or revise any prior trajectory.
requires_training: none — purely few-shot in-context prompting on off-the-shelf models. The paper explicitly states: 'No language models were finetuned in the process of writing this paper.'
reward_or_critic_model: none — there is no reward model, critic, or judge. The model directly emits the reasoning chain and answer; correctness is not scored or used as signal during inference.
distillation_target: none — reflection/experience is not distilled into any reusable artifact. The only reusable artifact is the small set of hand-written CoT exemplars (~8 exemplars) used in the prompt, which is engineered by humans rather than learned.
emergent_vs_engineered: Hybrid framing: the eliciting method (few-shot CoT exemplars in the prompt) is prompt/scaffold-engineered, but the underlying reasoning ability is an emergent ability of model scale (only appears at ~100B+ parameters per Wei et al. 2022b 'Emergent abilities'). The behavior is engineered-to-elicit but emergent-in-capability; it is NOT RL-emergent (predates R1-style 'aha' moments).
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad — the chain of thought acts as a within-prompt scratchpad / reasoning workspace; intermediate steps are written out in the generated text. No external or persistent memory store.
memory_persistence: within-episode — the reasoning trace exists only within the single generation for one problem; nothing persists across problems, episodes, or sessions.
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a — there is no accumulating memory to curate; each problem is solved with the same fixed human-written exemplar set and a fresh scratchpad.
error_localization_granularity: step-level (descriptive, not corrective) — the chain decomposes a problem into intermediate steps, and the paper's error analysis localizes failures to individual steps (e.g., 'one reasoning step missing', 'calculator/symbol-mapping error', 'semantic understanding error'). However, the method itself does not localize or correct errors; the step structure only enables post-hoc human error analysis.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task — reasoning happens within a single task instance. There is no cross-task experience transfer; the only cross-task element is the human-written exemplar prompt reused across the benchmark.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: n/a — no recovery or avoidance mechanism. CoT does not retry, recover mid-trajectory, or revise post-hoc; it produces one reasoning path with no guarantee of correctness ('there is no guarantee of correct reasoning paths').
task_domains: math (arithmetic word problems), QA/reasoning (commonsense reasoning), and symbolic reasoning; one decision-making/tool-use-adjacent task (SayCan robot action mapping).
benchmarks: Arithmetic: GSM8K, SVAMP, ASDiv, AQuA, MAWPS. Commonsense: CSQA, StrategyQA, Date Understanding (BIG-bench), Sports Understanding (BIG-bench), SayCan. Symbolic: Last-letter concatenation, Coin flip (with in-domain and OOD length-generalization splits).
headline_result: On GSM8K with PaLM 540B, CoT prompting (8 exemplars) raised solve rate from 18% (standard prompting) to 57%, achieving new state of the art and surpassing the prior best of a finetuned GPT-3 175B with a verifier (33%) and prior best (55%).
baselines: Standard few-shot prompting (input-output exemplars, direct answer; Brown et al. 2020) as the main same-model baseline; prior supervised/finetuned state-of-the-art models (e.g., finetuned GPT-3 175B + verifier from Cobbe et al. 2021 on GSM8K) and task leaderboards/human performance for commonsense tasks. Ablations: equation-only, variable-compute-only (dots), chain-of-thought-after-answer.
gains_vs_baseline: GSM8K PaLM 540B: 18% -> 57% (+39 pts, >3x). Performance more than doubled for the largest GPT and PaLM models on GSM8K. Commonsense: StrategyQA 75.6% vs 69.4% prior SOTA (+6.2 pts); Sports Understanding 95.4% vs 84% unaided human enthusiast; AQuA/ASDiv reach within 2% of SOTA; gain on CSQA was minimal. Symbolic in-domain reaches near-100% solve rate at 100B+ scale; CoT also enables OOD length generalization where standard prompting fails. Gains are an emergent ability of scale — negligible/negative below ~100B parameters.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-only; no training cost. CoT increases generated token count per query (intermediate reasoning steps) vs the direct-answer baseline, modestly raising inference cost/latency; the paper does not report a precise token multiplier. Single forward pass per problem (greedy decoding), so cost is roughly proportional to the longer output length, far cheaper than the sampling-based self-consistency follow-up. Main cost barrier is serving the 100B+ scale models at which CoT becomes effective.
known_limitations: (1) Does not establish whether the network is actually 'reasoning' — left as an open question. (2) Manual exemplar annotation is cheap few-shot but could be prohibitive for finetuning. (3) No guarantee of correct reasoning paths — can produce both correct answers via wrong reasoning and wrong answers; error analysis showed 54% of wrong-answer chains had major semantic/coherence errors. (4) Emergent only at large (~100B+) scale, making it costly to serve and ineffective for small models (small models produce fluent but illogical chains). (5) Sensitivity/variance to exemplars and prompt style (mitigated but present).
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: intrinsic-only — CoT uses no external feedback, verifier, oracle label, or environment reward at inference time. This is descriptive of the method (not a self-correction claim); CoT does not attempt to correct its own errors, so the Huang/Kamoi self-correction critique about needing oracle feedback does not directly apply, but it also means CoT has no error-correction guarantee.
self_correction_efficacy: n/a (not a self-correction method) — CoT does not perform self-correction; it improves task accuracy by eliciting reasoning, not by detecting/repairing errors. There is no correction step that could degrade or improve, so net efficacy of self-correction is not applicable.
calibration_effect: not-measured — the paper does not evaluate confidence calibration or report a 'reasoning tax'. Its analysis focuses on answer accuracy and error-type breakdowns, not calibration.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — CoT is not a failure-attribution method. The paper performs manual error analysis (categorizing wrong-answer chains into 'almost correct / minor mistake' ~46% vs 'major semantic/coherence error' ~54%, and showing scaling 62B->540B fixes one-step-missing and semantic errors), but provides no automated failure-mode classifier or attribution mechanism.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets/exposes multi-step reasoning failures: arithmetic computation errors, missing reasoning steps, and semantic-understanding/coherence breakdowns in step-by-step problem solving. In MAST terms it is closest to mitigating shallow/no-decomposition reasoning; conversely, small-scale CoT exhibits the failure of producing fluent-but-illogical chains (a 'superficial reasoning' analogue).
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new reusable benchmark or trace dataset released. The paper evaluates on existing public benchmarks and releases hand-crafted CoT exemplar prompts in the appendix (Tables 20-21, Appendix G/H) as a reusable prompting resource.
builds_on: Ling et al. 2017 (natural-language rationales for math word problems); Cobbe et al. 2021 (GSM8K dataset, finetuned verifier); Nye et al. 2021 (scratchpad / step-by-step intermediate computation); Brown et al. 2020 (few-shot in-context prompting / GPT-3); related instruction/prompting work (Wei et al. 2022a FLAN, Sanh et al. 2022, Ouyang et al. 2022). Conceptually grounded in Wei et al. 2022b (Emergent abilities of LLMs).
extended_by_or_inspired: Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2022, arXiv 2203.11171, sample multiple CoT + majority vote); Zero-shot CoT 'Let's think step by step' (Kojima et al. 2022); Least-to-Most prompting (Zhou et al. 2022); Automatic CoT / Auto-CoT (Zhang et al. 2022); Tree-of-Thoughts (Yao et al. 2023); ReAct (Yao et al. 2022, reasoning+acting); PAL/Program-aided reasoning; Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023) and Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) which add reflective/self-correction loops on top of CoT-style reasoning; o1/R1-style reasoning-trained models that internalize CoT.
citation_count: Approximately 16,900 (Semantic Scholar reports ~16,927 citations as of 2025-2026); one of the most-cited LLM prompting papers.
reasoning_model_native: No — predates and does not target o1/R1-style models with built-in/RL-trained reflection. CoT here is an externally elicited few-shot prompting technique on standard (non-reasoning-trained) base LLMs (GPT-3, LaMDA, PaLM). Later reasoning models internalize CoT into their weights via training, but that is downstream of this paper.
on_policy_distillation_link: None directly — this paper performs no distillation and no on-policy training. It is, however, a conceptual precursor: subsequent on-policy/skill-distillation work (e.g., distilling CoT traces into smaller models, RL on reasoning traces, reasoning-trace SFT) treats CoT-style traces as the data substrate to distill, but the CoT paper itself involves no weight updates or policy optimization.
sample_efficiency: Extremely sample-efficient at the prompt level: ~8 hand-written CoT exemplars (4 for AQuA) elicit the gains, with no training examples or gradient updates. Single forward pass per test problem (no retries/iterations). The 'cost' is shifted to model scale (~100B+ parameters required) rather than number of trials.
